title: "ClinVar submitters as a rater study"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{ClinVar submitters as a rater study}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", error = FALSE, cache = FALSE)
library(llmsa)
documentation <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
sys.source(system.file("validation", "m1d", "findings.R", package = "llmsa", mustWork = TRUE),
           envir = documentation)
anchors <- documentation$m1d_resources()
classes <- unlist(anchors[["ANK-47"]]$value$classes, use.names = FALSE)
read_submissions <- function(path) {
  con <- gzfile(path, "rt")
  on.exit(close(con), add = TRUE)
  utils::read.csv(con, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = "", encoding = "UTF-8")
}
datasets <- list(
  hrf = read_submissions(system.file("extdata", "clinvar_2026-10-19", "hrf_submissions.csv.gz",
                                    package = "llmsa", mustWork = TRUE)),
  sample = read_submissions(system.file("extdata", "clinvar_2026-10-19", "sample_submissions.csv.gz",
                                       package = "llmsa", mustWork = TRUE)))
as_rater_runs <- function(d) {
  as_msa_runs(data.frame(item_id = as.character(d$variation_id), prompt_id = d$submitter_id,
                         model_id = "clinvar", rep = 1L, value = d$classification))
}
```

These two public-domain subsets use ClinVar state **`r anchors[["ANK-41"]]$value$stand`**.
The HRF subset includes variants in MEFV, MVK, NLRP3 and TNFRSF1A with at least
two distinct submitters after the exact five-class filter. The genome-wide
sample draws **`r anchors[["ANK-47"]]$value$n_variants` variants** with at least
**`r anchors[["ANK-47"]]$value$min_distinct_submitters` distinct remaining submitters**,
using seed **`r anchors[["ANK-47"]]$value$seed`** from a numerically sorted list.
Filtering precedes both counting and sampling. Each selected variant retains
all qualifying submissions, including multiple SCVs from the same submitter.

The ordered scale is `r paste(classes, collapse = " < ")`. Other terms are
excluded, with counts in the packaged provenance. Gene lists come unchanged
from `variant_summary`; the submitter identifier is the original submitter
text. `data-raw/make_clinvar_subsets.R` checks the anchored source hashes and
reproduces the stored files. Their `SHA256SUMS` includes `QUELLE.txt`. This
article reads only installed data and makes no model calls.

## Agreement and ordinal components

Variant maps to item and submitter to prompt, with a single model and block,
and replicate one. Krippendorff's alpha uses all submissions without modal
reduction: `weights = "unweighted"` gives nominal alpha and `weights = "linear"`
selects the ordinal metric. The reported row is `all conditions`, whose unit
is the variant. Only variants with at least two submissions contribute
pairable ratings.

Complete agreement means the same one of the five classes for every
submission. Conflict means at least two of the three groups B/LB, VUS and
P/LP, following ANK-46. Both proportions use variants with at least two
submissions as denominator. Conflict is therefore not the complement of
complete agreement: a B/LB or P/LP difference fails exact agreement without
crossing a conflict boundary.

```{r agreement-and-fits}
alpha_values <- function(d) {
  runs <- as_rater_runs(d)
  nominal <- msa_agreement(runs, levels = classes, weights = "unweighted")
  ordinal <- msa_agreement(runs, levels = classes, weights = "linear")
  c(alpha_nominal = nominal$alpha$alpha[nominal$alpha$scope == "all conditions"],
    alpha_ordinal = ordinal$alpha$alpha[ordinal$alpha$scope == "all conditions"])
}
pairable_counts <- function(d) {
  sizes <- table(d$variation_id)
  c(variants = length(sizes), submissions = nrow(d), pairable_variants = sum(sizes >= 2L),
    pairable_submissions = sum(sizes[sizes >= 2L]))
}
groups <- setNames(c("B/LB", "B/LB", "VUS", "P/LP", "P/LP"), classes)
analyses <- lapply(names(datasets), function(name) {
  d <- datasets[[name]]
  ratings <- split(d$classification, d$variation_id)
  ratings <- ratings[lengths(ratings) >= 2L]
  agreement <- mean(vapply(ratings, function(x) length(unique(x)) == 1L, logical(1)))
  conflict <- mean(vapply(ratings, function(x) length(unique(groups[x])) >= 2L, logical(1)))
  diagnostics <- character()
  fit <- withCallingHandlers(msa_fit(as_rater_runs(d), type = "ordinal", levels = classes,
                                    interactions = FALSE, link = "probit"),
    warning = function(w) {
      diagnostics <<- c(diagnostics, conditionMessage(w)); invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }, message = function(m) {
      diagnostics <<- c(diagnostics, conditionMessage(m)); invokeRestart("muffleMessage")
    })
  grr <- msa_grr(fit)
  components <- setNames(fit$vc$variance, fit$vc$source)
  list(agreement = data.frame(subset = name, as.list(pairable_counts(d)), as.list(alpha_values(d)),
                              full_agreement = agreement, conflict = conflict),
       fit = data.frame(subset = name, item = components[["item"]], prompt = components[["prompt"]],
         grr_pct_study_var = grr$summary[["grr_pct_study_var"]], converged = fit$converged, singular = fit$singular),
       diagnostics = data.frame(subset = name, diagnostic = if (length(diagnostics)) paste(unique(diagnostics), collapse = " | ") else "none"))
})
```

```{r agreement-tables, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
for (part in c("agreement", "fit", "diagnostics")) {
  print(knitr::kable(documentation$m1d_display(do.call(rbind, lapply(analyses, `[[`, part))), row.names = FALSE))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

The fits use the default probit link without interactions. `item` is variant
variance; `prompt` is submitter variance. Percent GRR uses study variation.
The residual variance is fixed by the link, not an empirical estimate of
repeatability between submissions. Unbalanced participation, correlated
submissions from the same laboratory and differences in the assessed evidence
limit an interpretation as independent random raters. This is an agreement
study, not a clinical validation of individual classifications.

## Sensitivity to review status

The specified sensitivity keeps only statuses beginning literally with
**"criteria provided"**. It does not match "no assertion criteria provided".
It also excludes the higher status "reviewed by expert panel" and excludes
"flagged submission". The following counts show which statuses are present
and retained. The initial submitter thresholds are not applied again;
variants with one remaining submission cannot contribute to alpha.

```{r review-status-sensitivity}
status_counts <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(datasets), function(name) {
  counts <- as.data.frame(table(review_status = datasets[[name]]$review_status),
                          responseName = "submissions", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  data.frame(subset = name, counts, retained = startsWith(counts$review_status, "criteria provided"))
}))
sensitivity <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(datasets), function(name) {
  d <- datasets[[name]]
  d <- d[!is.na(d$review_status) & startsWith(d$review_status, "criteria provided"), , drop = FALSE]
  data.frame(subset = name, as.list(pairable_counts(d)), as.list(alpha_values(d)))
}))
```

```{r sensitivity-tables, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
print(knitr::kable(status_counts, row.names = FALSE))
cat("\n\n")
print(knitr::kable(documentation$m1d_display(sensitivity), row.names = FALSE,
                   caption = "Criteria-provided sensitivity: actual retained and pairable denominators."))
```

## Literature comparison

This comparison is **not an acceptance criterion**. All values below are read
from whole, hash-verified copies of ANK-42 through ANK-46. Counts, percentages,
alpha and reported bounds retain their units. The labelled quantity paths
identify each population and denominator; they should not be pooled into one
agreement rate.

Yang et al. (ANK-42) combine classes into three pathogenicity groups or two
actionability groups. Their clinical-testing subset from the later submission
period uses actionability, not exact five-class concordance. Their complete
agreement and majority-consensus rates answer different questions from each
other and from the stricter complete agreement computed here.

Amendola et al. (ANK-43) compare laboratory criteria and ACMG-AMP criteria,
then reassess agreement after consensus discussion. Their alpha population
differs from the population of the initial and post-discussion counts, and
the publication does not explicitly identify the alpha metric as nominal or
ordinal. Harrison et al. (ANK-44) distinguish exact agreement, differences
within B/LB or P/LP, and conflicts across those groups. Their reassessment
changes the evidence and cannot be treated as a replicate of this snapshot.

Lazareva et al. (ANK-46) study whether a variant was tagged with a conflict
at least once over the period **`r anchors[["ANK-46"]]$value$period`**, across
genes with disease associations. That cumulative proportion is not a
cross-sectional conflict fraction among multiply submitted variants.

Van Gijn et al. (ANK-45) provide the HRF comparison through a staged expert
consensus workflow. The first-round no-consensus percentage is a lower bound,
and the validation percentage is a voting rule. The abstract reports
`r anchors[["ANK-45"]]$value$consensus_final$variants` consensus variants out of
`r anchors[["ANK-45"]]$value$consensus_final$of`, while the Results counts sum to
`r anchors[["ANK-45"]]$value$validated$variants + anchors[["ANK-45"]]$value$provisional$variants`
from the validated and provisional groups. ANK-45 records this discrepancy;
the table preserves the reported abstract value. No INSAID classification
for an individual variant is distributed or used here.

```{r literature-tables, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
authors <- c("ANK-42" = "Yang et al.", "ANK-43" = "Amendola et al.", "ANK-44" = "Harrison et al.",
             "ANK-45" = "Van Gijn et al. (HRF)", "ANK-46" = "Lazareva et al.")
for (id in names(authors)) {
  a <- anchors[[id]]
  cat("\n### ", id, ": ", authors[[id]], "\n\n", sep = "")
  cat("Source: [", authors[[id]], "](", a$source_url, ").\n\n", sep = "")
  print(knitr::kable(documentation$m1d_display(documentation$m1d_literature_table(a), digits = 15L), row.names = FALSE))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

Agreement with other submitters is not a correctness label for a variant.
The different populations, grouping rules and reassessment procedures explain
why these literature results are contextual comparisons rather than target
values for either frozen subset. See `vignette("validation")` for the
statistical engine checks and the ordinal simulation findings.
